title: Chicago food inspections
summary: Predict whether a restaurant inspection will cite a given municipal code section - 40 binary task instances over 1.2 GB of Chicago's inspection record, with a frozen per-code split.

post.title: A citation-prediction task from Chicago's inspection record
paragraphs: The City of Chicago publishes every food inspection it conducts, including the code sections cited. Access is not the contribution. The contribution is the frozen panel - 226,417 inspections split 156,841 train / 35,358 eval / 34,218 holdout - the declaration that the prediction instant is the moment the inspection begins, and features computed only from that establishment's strictly earlier history.

The release carries 40 task instances, one per cited code section, delivered as separate configs. Each config asks the same question with its own label: will this inspection cite section X? Prevalence varies enormously by section, from 0.15% to 56.1%, so accuracy is meaningless here and AUC is the only honest score.

The numbers ship with their floor. Across the 40 configs the eval AUC runs 0.5187 to 0.8292, median 0.7208. On 38 of 40 configs the model beats a persistence reference - yesterday's presence of the same code - by +0.028 to +0.247 AUC; on two it does not, and those two are recorded rather than hidden. One config, code_38, was reproduced three times independently (0.6326) including from the published bytes in a fresh environment with no factory access.

limitations: A derived research dataset from the City of Chicago Data Portal, built under the City's Data Terms of Use, labelled as derived - not an official City of Chicago product.
Two of 40 configs (code_14 and code_32) do not beat their persistence reference. Recorded in measurements.json rather than left to be discovered.
Label prevalence spans 0.15% to 56.1% across configs. Score AUC; accuracy is misleading on the sparse configs.
The holdout is labelled and downloadable. Keep its labels outside the evaluated agent's workspace during an evaluation.
The source is the live register: a future refresh will not reproduce this exact panel, which is why the artifact version is pinned in the manifest.
